content: I was reading the paper on Hefty algebras and tried my hand in writing a Lean version, but the Agda encoding requires a universe shrinking in order for the paper's main type to typecheck. I was thinking that maybe the announced Shrink for the Iterators API might be able to perform this sort of task. Do we have some contenders for what this Shrink type will be?

Do you need to compile the code? If not, then the API around docs#Small and docs#Shrink should work.

If you need compilation, there is some discussion at lean4#9508, but many of the ideas discussed there don't work or introduce miscompilations. The topic is very subtle.
Thank you for the answer! Yes, ideally the code should be compiled because it is an encoding of algebraic effects and higher-order effects. I will be browsing the linked discussion, ty!

To reinforce Julia's point, you can build your own computable, unsafe Shrink, but there's no guarantee that the compiled code will behave; there could be bad interactions with optimizations. That is also the reason why we didn't implement it in the standard library yet.
If you're okay not to have guarantees, this thread contains concrete approaches for implementing an unsafe Shrink.

I see, thank you for the comment and the reference! Does it seem like the only way to go about this necessarily is as an opaque wrapper around an unsafe/external implementation?

EDIT: ah I wrote this before opening the thread and saw your comments there. Thanks again for the link!

Paul Reichert said:

If you're okay not to have guarantees, this thread contains concrete approaches for implementing an unsafe Shrink.

I think this is a bit of an understatement, given that the implementation suggested there introduces a known miscompilation (i.e., is native_decide-unsound): #general > Cardinality model incompatible with Lean compiler @ 💬

nrs said:

Does it seem like the only way to go about this necessarily is as an opaque wrapper around an unsafe/external implementation?

I think it's more likely that specific compiler support will be added for this feature or a generalization.
